---
title: "Computation time"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE)
```

```{r data}
bm <- utils::read.csv(system.file("benchmark", "results", "benchmark.csv",
                                  package = "simFastBOIN"),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
designs <- unique(bm$design)
rows_of <- function(d, impl) bm$design == d & bm$implementation == impl
med <- function(d, impl) stats::median(bm$seconds[rows_of(d, impl)])
first_of <- function(d, impl, col) bm[[col]][rows_of(d, impl)][1]
two <- function(x) prettyNum(signif(x, 2), big.mark = ",")
trials <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
show <- function(df) knitr::kable(df, row.names = FALSE)

has_ref <- designs[vapply(designs, function(d) {
  any(rows_of(d, "reference"))
}, logical(1))]
no_ref <- setdiff(designs, has_ref)
# TITE-gBOIN-ET is timed against two references.
n_ref_designs <- length(unique(sub(", program of the article$", "", has_ref)))
with_ref <- data.frame(
  design = has_ref,
  n_trials = vapply(has_ref, first_of, numeric(1), impl = "simFastBOIN",
                    col = "n_trials"),
  ref_fun = vapply(has_ref, first_of, "", impl = "reference", col = "fun"),
  ref_s = vapply(has_ref, med, numeric(1), impl = "reference"),
  ours_fun = vapply(has_ref, first_of, "", impl = "simFastBOIN",
                    col = "fun"),
  ours_s = vapply(has_ref, med, numeric(1), impl = "simFastBOIN"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
with_ref$ratio <- with_ref$ref_s / with_ref$ours_s
alone <- data.frame(
  design = no_ref,
  n_trials = vapply(no_ref, first_of, numeric(1), impl = "simFastBOIN",
                    col = "n_trials"),
  ours_fun = vapply(no_ref, first_of, "", impl = "simFastBOIN", col = "fun"),
  ours_s = vapply(no_ref, med, numeric(1), impl = "simFastBOIN"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
ratio_of <- function(d) with_ref$ratio[with_ref$design == d]
ref_s_of <- function(d) with_ref$ref_s[with_ref$design == d]
ours_s_of <- function(d) {
  c(with_ref$ours_s, alone$ours_s)[c(with_ref$design, alone$design) == d]
}
env <- bm[1, ]
comb12 <- c("Comb-BOIN12", "TITE-Comb-BOIN12")
```

The simulation engines of the package are written in C++. This article
gives the time that each design takes to simulate the trials of one scenario
and to summarize their operating characteristics, on one machine. The times
are read from `inst/benchmark/results/benchmark.csv`, written by
`inst/benchmark/benchmark.R`.

## What is measured

The `r n_ref_designs` designs that were compared with a reference
implementation, in another R package or in the code of the authors of the
design, are run by both with the same settings and the same number of
trials: those of the comparison of the design in `inst/validation/` or
`inst/reproduce/`, or of the README for the BOIN design, with the number of
trials used there for the reference. TITE-gBOIN-ET is timed against two
references, 'boinet' and the R program of the supporting information of
Takeda et al. (2023), a script that runs all the settings of the article
and that is run here as published for one of them, with its own rules,
which differ from those of the package in the two points described in the
article "How the package is checked". The `r length(no_ref)` other designs
are run by the package alone, with the settings of the example in their
vignette and `r trials(max(alone$n_trials))` trials. The settings are
listed in the section "Settings" below.

The time is the elapsed time of one call. A fast call is repeated until the
repetitions take at least one second, and the time per call is kept. Every
time was measured `r max(bm$rep)` times, alternating between the two
implementations, and the tables give the median. Printed output and
warnings of the calls are discarded. The package was installed before it
was timed: `devtools::load_all()` compiles the C++ code without
optimization.

## The machine

The times were measured on `r env$date` under `r env$os`, on an
`r env$cpu` with `r env$cores` physical cores, with R `r env$r_version`.
The simulations of the package run on one core. The code of the authors of
BOIN-ETC (the GitHub repository `kakizume/BOINETC`) and the program of Takeda
et al. (2023) have no version; the versions of the packages were

```{r versions}
versions <- unique(bm[!is.na(bm$version), c("package", "version")])
names(versions) <- c("Package", "Version")
show(versions)
```

## Designs compared with a reference implementation

```{r with-ref}
show(data.frame(
  Design = with_ref$design, Trials = trials(with_ref$n_trials),
  "Reference" = with_ref$ref_fun, "Reference (s)" = two(with_ref$ref_s),
  "simFastBOIN" = with_ref$ours_fun, "simFastBOIN (s)" = two(with_ref$ours_s),
  "Times faster" = two(with_ref$ratio), check.names = FALSE
))
```

The package was between `r two(min(with_ref$ratio))` and
`r two(max(with_ref$ratio))` times faster than the reference
implementation. The ratio is smallest for the three drug-combination
designs: `r two(ratio_of("BOIN combination"))` for the BOIN drug-combination
design, `r two(ratio_of("Waterfall"))` for the waterfall design and
`r two(ratio_of("BOIN-ETC"))` for BOIN-ETC. For the first two, both packages
select the MTD of every trial with the bivariate isotonic regression of
`Iso::biviso()`, called from R once per trial. The code of the authors of
BOIN-ETC simulates the trials and writes them to a file, and selects the
optimal dose combinations afterwards with another function, `CALC.SUM()`,
which is not timed; the package does both. The ratio is largest for
BF-BOIN-ET, whose reference implementation takes
`r two(ref_s_of("BF-BOIN-ET"))` seconds for
`r trials(with_ref$n_trials[with_ref$design == "BF-BOIN-ET"])` trials.

## Other designs

```{r alone}
show(data.frame(
  Design = alone$design, Trials = trials(alone$n_trials),
  "simFastBOIN" = alone$ours_fun, "Seconds" = two(alone$ours_s),
  check.names = FALSE
))
```

Other implementations exist for some of these designs, such as the
'TITEgBOIN' package for TITE-BOIN, but they were not compared with the
package and are not timed here. `r sum(alone$ours_s < 1)` of the
`r nrow(alone)` designs take less than one second for
`r trials(max(alone$n_trials))` trials. Comb-BOIN12 and
TITE-Comb-BOIN12 take about `r two(ours_s_of(comb12[1]))` and
`r two(ours_s_of(comb12[2]))` seconds: by default
(`est_method = "logistic"`) they estimate the response probabilities at the
end of every trial by the posterior mean under the logistic model of Lu et
al. (2025), computed by importance sampling with 4,000 points
(`n_draws = 4000`). With `est_method = "observed"`, the observed response
rates, the selection is much faster.

## Settings

```{r settings}
settings <- unique(bm[, c("design", "setting")])
names(settings) <- c("Design", "Setting")
show(settings)
```

The scripts named in the settings are in `inst/validation/` and
`inst/reproduce/`, from which the scenarios of the articles are also taken.

## Measuring on your own machine

From the root of the source package, install the package, restart R and run

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
library(simFastBOIN)
source("inst/benchmark/benchmark.R")
res <- run_benchmark(boinetc_zip = "path/to/BOINETC-main.zip",
                     takeda2023_zip = "path/to/Takeda_2023_SI.zip")
```

with the reference packages 'BOIN', 'boinet', 'bfboinet',
'UnifiedDoseFinding' and 'escalation' installed and the zip files of the
code of the authors of BOIN-ETC and of the supporting information of Takeda
et al. (2023); a design whose reference is missing is recorded as such. The
run writes
`inst/benchmark/results/benchmark.csv`. Most of the time goes to the
reference packages.

## References

Kakizume, T., Takeda, K., Taguri, M. and Morita, S. (2024). BOIN-ETC: A
Bayesian optimal interval design considering efficacy and toxicity to
identify the optimal dose combinations. *Statistical Methods in Medical
Research*, 33(4), 716-727.

Lu, M., Zhang, J., Yuan, Y. and Lin, R. (2025). Comb-BOIN12: A utility-based
Bayesian optimal interval design for dose optimization in cancer
drug-combination trials. *Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research*, 17(2),
266-276.

Takeda, K., Yamaguchi, Y., Taguri, M. and Morita, S. (2023). TITE-gBOIN-ET:
Time-to-event generalized Bayesian optimal interval design to accelerate
dose-finding accounting for ordinal graded efficacy and toxicity outcomes.
*Biometrical Journal*, 65(7), 2200265.
